content.thinking:
I'm planning the full character design in one pass: an Overwatch-style humanoid with a white/cream coat, teal bodysuit, coral accents, gold trim, and cyan glow, holding a staff with a winged head, plus a cyborg arm, working out orientation so the staff and mechanical limb are placed on the correct sides relative to the viewer.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton hierarchy -- spine chain from hips through chest to upper torso, then neck segments leading into a head joint, building each as parented chains with careful positioning so the proportions stay around 1.75m tall.

I'm adding a small jaw joint for facial detail, then moving to the arm structure: setting shoulder positions symmetrically, with the left arm (world +X) extending outward and forward toward an open robotic hand.

Now I'm placing the right arm so it holds a vertical staff, working out elbow and wrist coordinates by estimating segment lengths for the upper arm and forearm to keep proportions realistic.

I'll skip full IK and just build the arm as a simple joint chain of shoulder, elbow, and hand points connected by a polyline, parented to the spine, accepting the slight corner at the elbow as fine for this style.

For naming I'll append L/R based on side sign, and set up sweeps for the arm radius tapering from upper arm to forearm. I'll vary the sleeve colors by band—dark graphite for one arm's sleeve, cream or robotic white for the other—keeping the overall look clean in that Overwatch-inspired style.

Mostly I'm sticking with flat colors but adding a few subtle paints for texture: a soft mottled surface for the white armor piece and a custom panel-line treatment for the coat, plus a coral trim along the hem based on vertical position. Now I'm placing the leg joints—hips, knees, ankles—and setting up the foot chain with heel and toe positions for the boots.

I'm defining the leg joint chain with hip, knee, and ankle points, and deciding to add the toe as a separate joint parented to the ankle rather than extending the main chain, giving it a "digit" role so the foot geometry attaches cleanly without stretching the leg tube into the foot.

Now I'm sketching the boot geometry as an extruded profile in the z-y plane, outlining the foot shape from heel to toe with a side cross-section I'll sweep across the boot's width.

Still writing boot outline geometry...

Building spine chain stations for the torso loft...

I'm planning white sphere pairs for the breastplate and a coral shoulder cross pad, then sketching out a long white coat with asymmetrical hem and coral lining as separate extruded panels rigged to the hips bone so the tails flare outward.

Mapping out the coat panel's hanging outline now, defining a pointed hem shape that tapers down from the waist attachment point with a few vertices going from the shoulder down to a pointed tip around the hip area.

I'm designing the coat as a flared, cape-like garment with front and back tabard panels (cream with coral lining), side vents widening past the legs, plus a gold hem band and coral under-lining via a second thinner extrude layer.

Writing paint function for diagonal coral stripe...

I'm checking the thickness symmetry on the mirrored side and confirming panel offsets stay consistent. For the staff prop, I'm placing it vertical in her right hand, running from the floor up to about 1.95 units tall so it stands noticeably taller than her 1.75-unit frame.

I'm rigging the staff as a rigid attachment to the hand bone rather than giving it its own separate joint hierarchy, positioning its named joint near the hand at roughly (-0.42, 1.0, 0.3) pointing upward.

Now I'm detailing the staff's visual construction: a graphite shaft with white sleeves and gold rings, a cyan glow strip, a gold spiked ferrule with a gem at the bottom, and a crescent-winged head with layered cream and teal plates, a central spear blade, and a glowing orb wrapped in halo rings plus floating cyan crosses.

Still positioning staff geometry... Now I'm planning the cyborg arm design with white plates and glowing cyan joints, and working out the finger/hand joint structure within the budget.

For the left hand, I'm computing the wrist position and finger base offsets using vector math so the open palm gesture faces up and forward, with fingers spread laterally along the base direction.

For the right fist gripping the staff, I'm simplifying to a palm box with four curling finger chains wrapping around the staff cylinder, positioning the hand so the arm approaches from behind and the fingers close around from the back side through the front.

Deciding that's too much detail for finger rigging, I'll skip it and move on to defining the color palette instead—armor whites, teal and coral accents, gold trim, graphite details, cyan highlights, and skin and hair tones for the character.

For the face, I'm planning to draw a simple stylized eye with an almond shape, gradient iris, pupil highlight, and lash line via a small custom SVG decal, mirrored for the other eye, then figure out how to position it on the head's spherical surface using decal placement at a forward-facing point.

Now I'm working out the skull geometry: a scaled sphere for the head at roughly (0, 1.74, 0.03), a jaw piece positioned below it, plus small shapes for a nose, lips, and ears, and I'm planning the ponytail hair as swept bezier strands with clumps for bangs.

For the hair cap I'm thinking of using a partial sphere geometry (a top portion cut with theta/phi limits) positioned and scaled slightly larger than the skull to cover the top and back, shifted back a touch so the face stays uncovered, and tilting the cap so the hairline rim curves naturally across the forehead.

For the hairstyle itself, I'm planning side-swept front bangs as two tapering sweeps toward the ears, plus a wavy ponytail built from several bezier curve sweeps flowing from the back of the head upward and curling down, with slight color variation between strands for a messy, natural look.

I also want to add a gold headband arcing across the top of the head using a curved rod shape, positioned just above the hairline with a gem accent at the front-center, making sure it sits correctly relative to the skull's dimensions.

I'll settle on slightly lower band points to avoid floating too far above the hair surface, accepting the tilt makes the front naturally higher. With roughly 400 parts budgeted, I'm ready to move into writing the actual code.

I'm reconsidering the character's proportions — Overwatch-style heroic stylized, with a slightly taller build. I want to scale the head/hair/ponytail heights down so the total body height lands around 1.78-1.8, with the staff a bit taller at 2.15, then recompute the skeleton coordinates from there.

Working through joint positions — hips, knees, ankles, spine curve, neck, head/skull with hair and ponytail, shoulders, and arm chains for elbows and wrists on both sides.

Defining the arm chain joints...

Now I'm setting up the torso loft stations with chest, waist, and hip widths tapering appropriately, plus pauldron shoulder details, and considering adding a belt loop around the waist using a surface sweep.

Defining leg bone chains with hip, knee, and ankle joint positions for suit and armor plating...

Working out the thigh and leg armor plates, trying boxy frustum shapes versus capsule sweeps to get that chunky armored look while keeping the bone joints aligned between hip and knee.

Still defining knee and boot geometry...

I'll skip adding a separate toe joint since the humanoid rig works fine with just ankle and foot. Now I'm working out the coat panel placements around the hips, positioning front and back panels with slight offsets in depth so they flare naturally over the waist.

Working out the panel tilt vectors...

Now checking for collisions between the leg panels and thigh armor as the hem flares forward—comparing z-depths at hip versus hem height to make sure the panel clears the thigh, and confirming the two side panels meet at a center slit without overlapping badly.

I'm now setting up the back panels with a wider outline that flares outward more dramatically than the front, and adding a slimmer coral lining layer placed just behind each panel offset toward the body to peek out at the edges.

Next I'm working out a gold hem trim via a procedural paint function using coordinate values to create a diagonal coral stripe and gold line pattern on the coat surface.

I also want a center front teal apron panel running from the belt down to the knees, pointed at the tip with a gold edge outline, so I'm sketching out its symmetric vertex shape before extruding it.

For the chest I'm layering white overbust armor with scaled spheres, then adding a high standing teal/white collar around the neck via a lathe shape, bound to the neck joint bone. I might still add coral lapel pieces to round out the coat collar if there's room.

Now moving to shoulders: I'm building rounded white pauldrons using scaled spheres (slightly flattened for a plate-like look), positioned at each shoulder, with the character's left shoulder getting a flat coral cross decal placed toward the outer top of the pauldron.

For the right pauldron I'm going with a teal plate accented by a gold ring, plus matching gold rivet rings at both shoulders. Then I'm moving to the arm armor, starting with the left (cyborg) forearm as a white plated capsule with glowing cyan rings.

Elbow joint gets a dark sphere with a cyan ring glow, while the upper arm uses teal/graphite sleeve coloring. I'm working out the band placement along the arm's path using chain-source t-values—upper arm length 0.30, forearm 0.26, putting the elbow joint around t≈0.54—so I can split the sleeve into a dark upper section transitioning to white forearm with the cyan joint sphere. For the right arm, which holds the staff, I'm considering a cream sleeve with a dark gray glove.

I'm now setting up tan sleeve bands for the forearm with a dark glove, plus designing the left robotic hand with white palm and finger plates separated by small dark joint rings. I'm writing a helper function to place glowing cyan torus rings around the forearm at specific points, attached to bones with a given direction and radius.

I'm typing the bone parameter as Joint or Chain imported from the skeleton module, then wrapping parts with a glow effect for the cyan pieces. I'm also planning floating glowing plus-sign sparkles made from thin extruded cross shapes around the staff.

Now I'm positioning twelve plus-sign points near the staff head and adding a spiral healing ribbon swept around the staff using a spiral helper with configurable turns, radius, and pitch.

I'm defining the staff orb position and glow at the top of the shaft, then building the gold collar lathe shape and crescent blade outline to extrude for the staff head details.

Now I'm layering a second, teal inner blade shifted slightly forward in z for depth, and sketching the central spear point as a tall pointed polygon positioned at the shaft base.

Next I'm setting up a staff joint hinged at the hand's tip position, attaching it as the arm chain's terminal joint, then laying out the staff shaft as a rod running up from the base to grip height.

Then I'm adding details along the staff: a gold spike ferrule at the bottom touching the floor, and above it a glowing octahedral gem with small gold wing flanges decorating the lower body.

Continuing up, I'm placing white rod sleeves with gold banded rings and thin cyan glow slit strips at intervals (lower, mid, and near-hand sections), then finishing the upper portion near the top with diagonal gold wing plates for visual flourish.

I'm defining a reusable staffSleeve helper that lathes a bulbous collar profile with chunky kite-shaped segments in cream and gold, then building the hand grip itself—tori wrapped around the staff radius to form fingers, a thumb capsule, and a palm block positioned relative to the wrist.

For the fist, I'm deciding to just hide the staff inside a vertical skin-colored capsule centered at the forearm, letting the visible finger rings sit on the front while the rounded capsule shape covers where the hand actually grips.

Covering the fist in a dark fingerless glove on top, with skin-colored finger capsules showing across the front and a diagonal thumb capsule on the top-inside. Then I'm wrapping the right forearm in tan with a gold bracelet torus at the wrist.

Now moving to the left hand, I'm building the wrist position and arm chain, then computing the hand's bend direction so the palm angles forward and slightly upward, deriving a side axis for the finger placement.

In anatomical standing position with palms forward, thumbs point outward from the body, so for the left hand the thumb sits at +X and the pinky toward the body at −X. I'm setting lateral offsets for the four fingers accordingly.

Working out finger geometry now—spacing, segment lengths tapering from index through pinky, a slight spread, and curl applied per segment toward the palm normal. Naming each joint point for the finger chains...

Still defining thumb placement and the palm box orientation using the aim and up vectors...

For the back-of-hand I'm adding a cyan glowing disc on the palm surface and a gold torus ring at the wrist, both oriented along the hand's direction vector. I'm also noting that Vector3 values convert cleanly to arrays for the point data format.

Moving to the left arm, I'm placing a glowing cyan torus ring at the elbow with a dark sphere joint, then building forearm armor as a tapered capsule from elbow to wrist with additional thin cyan rings positioned at the 30% and 70% marks along its length.

Now I'm shifting to facial features, planning an almond-shaped eye with a layered iris, pupil, highlight, and lash details using an SVG with gradient fills and clipping to keep the iris contained within the eye shape.

Mirroring the eye decal for the opposite side, calculating its exact position on the skull surface using the head's curvature math, and confirming stroke widths and texture resolution for crisp rendering.

Now I'm working out the brow geometry: small curved sweep shapes using dark hair color, positioned near the skull surface above each eye, computing their depth coordinates against the head's curved profile at a couple of x-positions along the brow.

Next I'm placing the nose using a small cone primitive angled slightly forward and downward from center, positioning its tip to project beyond the face surface near the eye line.

Then I'm shaping the lips with a capsule-based rod stretching across the mouth width, colored coral-pink, positioned at the correct surface depth where the face curves inward.

Now I'm working out how the jaw sphere scales to form the chin, making sure it protrudes far enough forward so the lower lip has proper support, and splitting the lips so the upper one attaches to the head bone while the lower one attaches to the jaw bone for natural movement.

For the ears, I'm adding small skin-toned spheres with a tiny teal earpiece disc and gold torus ring on the left ear as a cyborg accent. For shading, I'm deciding against cel-shading in favor of flat colors with subtle gradient paint variants to match a softer, painted Overwatch-style look -- armor gets a slight gradient, fabric gets subtle noise mottling.

I'm defining countershade paints for armor (white lit top, shaded underneath) and the suit (teal with darker teal undertone), making sure glow parts stay flat strings and all parts get explicit colors. Then I'm working out the torso loft stations and the neck as a short polyline chain with tapering radius from the base up to the jaw.

I'm continuing to build out the skeleton—adding head and jaw joints with specific positions and aim directions, sweeping the neck geometry with a linear taper in skin tone, then setting up the hips as the root joint before the spine chain takes over the spine role.

Now I'm parenting leg chains to hips based on left/right side, sweeping the leg geometry with the bodysuit color, and adding pelvis and hip crotch spheres to fill the gap where torso and thighs meet, sized to match the torso's width at that station.

Adding hip armor plates as capsules at the sides, a glowing teal vial with gold caps as a belt pouch on the left hip, a white pouch box on the right hip, breast armor spheres on the chest, and a small cyan gem emblem at the sternum to mirror the reference art's chest ring detail.

I'm placing the sternum emblem as a torus with a cyan center, positioning it just in front of the chest loft surface between the breast plates so it reads clearly without clipping into the armor bulge. I'm skipping the slanted lapel idea in favor of keeping the chest plates as the main armor feature.

For the chest graphic itself, instead of modeling separate extruded stripes I'm using a decal mapped onto the curved torso surface with a coral V and gold trim design, sized to sit centered on the upper chest. I'm also considering adding a compact medical pack with cyan vents on the upper back, built from simple box geometry, to round out the costume detail.

Then I'm checking that every import I actually use is included and nothing unused slips through, since unused imports would cause errors once everything gets written out.

Adding more imports and defining metadata...

Adding box geometry helper...

Lit parts just use flat colors, that's fine. Now I'm setting up the skeleton with a hip joint and a spine chain built from a catmull curve through four points, with three spine segments defined between them—named spine1 through spine3 without a tip bone.

Continuing the chain, I'm defining a neck chain parented to the spine with two segments, then adding head and jaw joints. For the arms, I'm setting up polyline data for left and right arm points, building shoulder-elbow-hand chains parented to the spine—though I'm noticing the names array length doesn't quite match the number of path spans, so I need to adjust for the tip joint naming.

Setting up legs similarly...

Actually, if I pass a bone binding without specifying which joint, it defaults to the chain's tip joint — that's wrong for thigh armor since it'd ride with the ankle instead of the hip. I need to explicitly bind thigh pieces to the hip joint rather than letting it default to the last joint in the chain.

So I'm indexing the leg chain's joints array directly: joints[0] is the hip, [1] is the knee, [2] is the ankle, and I'll bind thigh armor to the hip joint, shin armor to the knee joint, and boot armor to the ankle joint. For the shin capsule geometry, I'm sizing it slightly larger than the leg's sweep radius so the armor sits just outside the limb, and adding an extra front plate for visual detail on the shin.

Now I'm working out the knee guard as a scaled ball joint, plus decorative rings: a cyan torus ring and a slightly larger gold torus ring positioned on the outer side of the knee, and matching rings on the thigh armor near its upper outer face, adjusting radius and tube thickness so they sit flush against the tapering armor surface.

For the boot, I'm adding a gold toe cap using a flattened sphere scaled to fit at the ankle/toe position, plus considering a gold ankle strap torus, making sure the boot shaft dimensions properly encase the leg bone radius underneath.

Adding boot cuff ring and sole details...

Now I'm plotting the coat's front panel outline point by point, tracing a shape that flares out from the waist down past the hip before curving back in near the knee, making sure the path stays simple and non-self-intersecting.

Working through the geometry, I check that the y direction's z-component pushes the back panel outward and backward as it descends, confirming the back-flaring behavior matches what's needed. I don't think perpendicularity between x and y panel axes is required here, and I'm now checking whether the front panel intersects correctly at the leg.

Tracing the panel hem position against the thigh and knee, the front panel ends up slightly below the knee, which is fine since the reference coat extends down to around knee/calf level. I want to trim the front panel length a bit though, so I'm adjusting the front outline's y-values to shorten the hem slightly.

For the coral lining, I'm scaling up the same outline slightly around the origin to create a thin visible edge peeking out from behind the coat panels.

Writing coat paint function...

Skipping the backpiece decal, I'll do the teal apron with a flat paint function adding gold trim along the edges. For the cyborg elements, I'm deciding to keep natural eyes but add a cybernetic ear piece, neck port, and full left arm, while considering whether both legs should also show armored cyborg detailing.

Now I'm designing the staff head geometry, placing a ferrule spike, a glowing octahedron gem in cyan, and gold flange shapes extruded outward from the shaft near the top collar point.

Adding sleeve and flange details...

Continuing sleeve segments up the staff with alternating white/gold bands and cyan accent strips, plus small gold wedge wing fins near the midsection for armor detailing. For the head, I'm lathing a flared gold collar near the top and capping it with a glowing cyan orb.

Now I'm caging the orb with three interlocking gold torus rings, then defining crescent blade shapes at the base with an outward-curving outline that tapers to a sharp tip before curving back in, forming an asymmetric thickness band.

Adding a smaller teal inner crescent layer, gold spike tips at the points, and now shaping a center spear blade with a pinched diamond outline and a thinner teal inset.

Still defining the spiral ribbon geometry...

Now I'm working out how the right hand's fingers should wrap around the staff—figuring out whether the fist curls with knuckles facing forward given the forearm's angle coming from behind and above the grip point.

I'm recalculating the right arm's joint positions, adjusting the wrist closer to the staff and checking elbow placement so the forearm and upper-arm segment lengths stay proportional to the left arm.

Then I'm placing the fist and fingers wrapping around the staff: the palm block sits just behind the staff, while four finger tori encircle it like rings, sized slightly larger than the staff's radius for a natural grip.

I'm also adding a thumb capsule angled across the top of the fist to complete the hold, checking that the finger rings don't collide awkwardly with the palm box geometry.

Now I'm adding a gold wrist bracelet torus on the forearm sleeve, oriented perpendicular to the arm direction with a thin tube radius, then moving on to hair construction using bezier sweep paths for the cap, bangs, ponytail, and side strands.

Working out the ponytail curve control points with tapering radius, then sketching side locks swept from the part down to the cheeks and a big side-swept front bang across the forehead, each defined by catmull-rom curves with decreasing radius toward the tips.

Now I'm shaping the hair cap itself as a scaled, rotated sphere segment slightly larger than the skull so it fully covers it, positioning it just above and behind the head with the rim tucked under near the back.

I'm catching an inconsistency in my skull center value — I had used 1.74 in one calc but 1.63 elsewhere, which threw off the cap top position. Let me redo the skull geometry with center at (0,1.63,0.035) and the correct scale factors to get an accurate top point around y=1.727.

Now I'm adjusting the cap placement to sit just above the skull center at (0,1.64,0.02), checking that the hemisphere's tilt angle (-35°) gives a front rim around eye-level height of 1.70 and a back rim near 1.58, which matches a natural hairline position rather than sitting too low at eye level.

Side hair at the ear region needs checking too -- ears sit around x±0.082-0.09, and since rotation is only on the x-axis, the sides stay unaffected by the tilt, so the cap's radius should naturally cover the ear area near the rim at y=1.64. I'll settle on a -32° tilt with a full hemisphere shape, confirming the open rim interior stays hidden behind the skull geometry so no visible gap shows through.

For hair color I'm using a grain texture over the HAIR material to give it strand-like variation, sized small and aligned along the y-axis for a natural look. Now I'm positioning a golden headband as a curve along the cap surface near the hairline, picking a handful of points that arc from each side up to the crown, estimating z and y coordinates so the tube radius is generous enough to read correctly whether it sits slightly embedded or floating above the cap.

I'm placing a small teal gem at the center of the headband, giving it a faint cyan glow to make it pop. For cyborg detailing, I'm adding a small white panel with a thin cyan line near the left temple to hint at a mechanical implant, sizing it as a thin box geometry positioned against the skull surface.

Now I'm sketching an SVG decal for the chest—a coral chevron shape with a gold V-stroke accent—though I realize the chevron sits between the breast spheres where it may get obscured, so I'll need to reposition it to actually show in the gap.

I'm also planning a hip-mounted teal glowing vial, a small cylinder with gold caps and a slight tilt, attached by a strap sweep near the belt line.

For the belt itself, I'm figuring out the surface loop around the torso at the waist, sweeping a closed path for the belt band, then adding a gold disc buckle positioned right at the belt's front, calculating the exact z-depth so it sits just above the surface.

Now I'm shifting to left arm construction, computing shoulder, elbow, and wrist points as vectors to build the arm chain.

Deciding to use flat white for the sweep tube and paint fills for armor parts, then starting to lay out the left forearm armor capsule geometry.

Still placing joint spheres and armor bands...

Still writing finger geometry...

Still writing hand geometry...

For the palm I'm adding a box with a dorsal plate, and deciding to skip finger joints on the right hand since it's not fully rigged. For the shoulder pads, I'm attaching them near the arm's upper joint with a sphere and a gold rim torus around the base.

I'll build a rivet helper that merges small gold spheres into one mesh for belts, boots, and the coat, then add a cross decal onto the left shoulder pad only.

For the cross shape, I'm designing a simple SVG cross icon in coral with a white outline, sized to apply as a decal texture on the backpack plane, keeping its own coloring separate from the part's base color. Now I'm thinking about adding white armor plates near the hip/pelvis area using capsule shapes.

For the hips, I'll add small ball-scaled armor plates plus a gold ring torus, finalize the collar design using a lathe shape with a teal body and gold rim ring rather than extruded lapels, and then check overall proportions—boots at floor level, head/ponytail height around 1.75-1.83, staff tip near 2.27—before estimating the total joint count for the rig.

Now I'm mapping out the boot construction: extruding the boot outline with bevel and smoothing set carefully to avoid geometry errors, then adding gold toe accents, teal soles, ankle straps with buckles, heel guards, and a glowing laces detail on the shaft front.

Setting up helper functions to simplify part creation, with typed color and bone parameters so I can quickly instantiate spheres and other primitives throughout the rig.

Checking that glow works fine on flat-colored parts since it needs a single standard material, and confirming texture strings won't break it since only flat colors are used here.

Now I'm working out the staff joint hierarchy on the arm chain, and setting up the eye decal on the skull part. I'm also mapping out the coat panel extrusion loops for the front and back, figuring out the offsets for each side's outline positioning.

Still placing the lining and panel depths...

Skipping the gold trim for now since paint covers it. I'm defining a spiral helper for staff geometry and a plus-sign extrusion function that generates outline points scaled to the glyph size, glowing cyan along the staff bone. Now I'm sketching an SVG eye texture with a clip path for the finishing details.

Still writing eye and eyelid strokes...
